title: SPEAK PSALM 23 INTO YOUR LIFE THIS MORNING
text: Somebody open your mouth and say good morning to the Almighty God. I said open your mouth, lift your head and greet the King of glory this morning because this is not an ordinary gathering. This is not a casual devotion. This is a divine appointment and heaven has been waiting for this exact moment to locate you. Before you scroll past, before you rush into your day, the Holy Ghost has stopped you right here because he wants to speak into your life through a psalm that has carried kings through war, that has carried widows through grief, that has carried the sick through hospital corridors, that has carried the broke through seasons of lack. And that psalm is Psalm 23. Today, we are not just going to read it. We are not just going to recite it the way you learned it in Sunday school. We are going to speak it. We are going to decree it. We are going to let it rise up from your belly like rivers of living water until every line becomes a living reality working in your life. Hallelujah. Somebody shout hallelujah like you mean it. Let me take you back. This song was not written by a theologian sitting comfortably in a library. [music] This was written by a man who had smelled the breath of lions, who had chased down a bear with his bare hands to rescue a lamb. who had stood in a valley with five smooth [music] stones facing a giant that made an entire army tremble. Who had slept in caves running from a king who wanted him dead. Who had buried friends. Who had wept over a rebellious son. Who had known betrayal from men who ate at his table. David did not write Psalm 23 from a place of fury. He wrote [music] it from a place of testimony. When David says, "The Lord is my shepherd," he's not quoting a verse. He's recounting a relationship. He's telling you what he has personally experienced in the wilderness, in the war, in the wandering. And this morning, the Holy Spirit is asking you, can you say the same thing? Not what your pastor said, not what you read on a poster, but what have you personally tasted of this shepherd? The Lord is my shepherd. Stop right there. Not the Lord was my shepherd yesterday when things were fine. Not the Lord will be my shepherd when I finally sort myself out. The Lord is my shepherd. Present tense. Right now, in the middle of your unpaid bills, in the middle of your medical report, in the middle of your marital storm, in the middle of your business uncertainty, in the middle of your job search that seems to be going nowhere right now, this morning, in your exact situation, he is your shepherd. A shepherd does not abandon the sheep in the middle of danger. A shepherd does not disappear when the wolves show up. A true shepherd, the kind David is describing, lays down his [music] life for the sheep. And I want you to know that Jesus himself picked up this very psalm and wore it like a garment when he said, "I am the good shepherd." The good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. So when you say, "The Lord is my shepherd," you are not talking about a distant dity watching from far off. You are talking about a shepherd who bled, who was pierced, who was wounded for your transgressions, who carried stripes so that by his stripes you would be healed. This is not a fairy tale shepherd. This is a shepherd who knows the terrain of your suffering because he walked through it himself. And because he is my shepherd, David says, I shall not want. Now catch this. Because this is where many of us stumble in our understanding. I shall not want does not mean nothing will ever come against you. It does not mean you will never face a valley [music] because the very same psalm mentions a valley later on. What it means is that in the hand of this shepherd, [music] lack has no final authority over your life. Whatever you are lacking this morning, whether it is peace, whether it is provision, whether it is direction, whether it is healing, whether it is a testimony, whether it is a husband, whether it is a child, whether it is clarity for the next step, I decree to you that because the shepherd is alive, that lack is temporary and it is already scheduled for reversal. Somebody needs to shout it out loud this morning. I shall not want. Say it again. with fire in your belly. I shall not want because my father owns the cattle on a thousand hills. Because my father is Jehovah Gyra, the God who sees ahead and makes provision before the need even arrives. He saw your today from eternity and he has already stocked heaven's storehouse with everything your today would require. So stop begging like an orphan. Stop striving like someone with no father. Lift up your head. You are a child of the shepherd and where he leads provision [music] follows. He makes me to lie down in green pastures. Notice he says he makes me. Sometimes you will not choose the rest. Sometimes you are so consumed with huzzling, so consumed with striving, so consumed with running from meeting to meeting, from hospital to church to work to family drama that if the shepherd does not forcefully make you lie down, you will run yourself into the grave trying to fix everything with your own strength. This morning I speak to every overworked, overwhelmed, overstretched soul. The shepherd is saying, "Come aside. Lie down. Let me handle what has been eating you alive." Green pastures do not grow in dry, [music] cost, forsaken land. Green pastures are evidence of divine cultivation. Wherever the shepherd leads you, he has already prepared nourishment for you there. That means the very location you think is delaying you, the very season you think is punishing you could actually be the pasture where God is fattening you for the next level of your assignment. He leads me beside the still waters. Not troubled waters, not waters of confusion, not waters of chaos, but still waters, quiet waters, waters that restore rather than waters that drown. If your spirit has been troubled, if your mind has been racing at 3:00 in the morning with anxiety, if you have been drinking from wells of bitterness and gossip and comparison and social media noise, the shepherd is calling you this morning to his still [music] waters. Come and drink from a source that will not leave you more thirsty than before. He restores my soul. Somebody say it with me. He restores my soul. This is not about your body only. This is about the deep parts of you. The parts that got wounded by rejection. The parts that got shattered by disappointment. The parts that got buried under shame from things you did or things that were done to you. Restoration means bringing back to the original design. Before the labels the world gave you, before the wounds life inflicted on you, before the lies the enemy planted in you, God had an original blueprint [music] for your soul. And this morning, he's picking up the broken pieces and putting them back exactly the way he intended. He leads me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Not for your name's sake, not because you are so wonderful, but for his [music] name's sake. Because his reputation is tied to your testimony. When God leads you out of that mess, when he turns your situation around, it is not just for you to celebrate. It is so that the name of the Lord will be glorified through your life. That should shift how you pray. You are not just asking for breakthrough for your own comfort. You are contending for breakthrough that will make his name great in the eyes of everyone watching your life. Then David takes a turn, and this is the part that many people skip past too quickly. Yay. Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil. Notice, it is a valley, not a permanent residence. You are only walking through it. Whatever valley you find yourself in this morning, whether it is a valley of sickness, a valley of financial pressure, a valley of grief, a valley of a relationship that shattered, a valley of a diagnosis that shook you, a valley of waiting so long you started to wonder if God forgot your address. I speak to that valley right now. You are a passage, not a destination. And the shepherd is walking through it with the sheep. Notice also it says shadow of death, not death itself. A shadow cannot kill you. A shadow has no teeth, no claws, no power to touch your body. The enemy can only throw shadows at you because Jesus already conquered the substance at Calvary. He disarmed principalities and powers and made a show of them openly. So whatever is casting a shadow over your health, over your finances, over your children, over your marriage, over your destiny, that thing has already been defeated in the spirit, and it can only intimidate you with [music] a shadow because it has no actual power left. I will fear no evil, for thou art with me. The presence of the shepherd is the antidote to fear. Fear cannot survive. where the manifest presence of God is welcomed. Thy rod and thy staff, they comfort me. The rod was for correction and defense. The staff was for guidance and rescue, pulling the ship back from cliffs, striking at predators. This morning, God is telling you, I am not just walking beside you as decoration. I am actively defending you. I am actively correcting your path when you veer off. I am actively rescuing you when you get too close to the edge. That should bring comfort to your spirit. You are not wandering alone in this valley. You have a shepherd with a rod in one hand [music] ready to strike anything that threatens you and a staff in the other hand ready to pull you back from every edge the enemy has set up to destroy you. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. I want you to see the audacity of this statement. God does not wait for your enemies to disappear before he blesses you. He sets up a banqueting table right there in full view of the very people who said you would never make it. In full view of the ones who mocked your dream. In full view of the family members who wrote you off. In full view of the colleagues who thought you were finished. In full view of the sickness that thought it had the final word. He prepares your table right there in the presence, not the absence of your enemies, so that they will be forced to watch your elevation while helpless to stop it. Thou anointest my head with oil. Oil in scripture speaks of fresh empowerment, of separation for divine purpose, of healing, of joy, replacing mourning. This morning I decree fresh oil upon your head, fresh anointing for the next assignment, fresh strength for the next battle, fresh joy to replace whatever grief has been sitting on your shoulders. My cup runth over. Not just enough, but overflow. [music] Not just survival, but abundance spilling out so that it touches everyone around you. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life. I love this line because it says, "Goodness and mercy are following you." Meaning they are chasing you down. They are pursuing you. They are relentlessly on your trail. Whatever you feel is chasing you this morning. Whether it is fear, whether it is debt, whether it is sickness, whether it is disappointment, I declare that goodness and mercy are running faster. And they about to overtake every negative thing that has been pursuing your life. All the days, not just on the good days, not just when you feel spiritual, but all the days, the difficult ones and the joyful ones. Goodness and mercy are attached to you like a shadow that never leaves. And I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever. This is not just about eternity in heaven someday, though that is glorious and sure. It is also about a settled, permanent, unshakable dwelling in the presence of God right now. A life anchored in him so deeply that no storm can dislodge you from that place. Now hear me church. Hear me wherever you are standing or sitting or lying down this morning because we are moving from teaching into declaration and I need you to open your mouth because faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God and you need to hear your own voice agreeing with heaven. Say after me out loud do not whisper declare it. The Lord is my shepherd and because he is my shepherd I shall not want in this season. I shall not want peace for he gives it beyond understanding. I shall not want provision for my father owns silver and gold. I shall not want direction for he leads me even when I cannot see the next step. I shall not want healing for by his stripes I am already healed. I shall not want companionship in my struggle for he never leaves me nor forsakes me. I decree over your finances this morning, [music] every closed door assigned to hinder your provision is broken right now in the name of Jesus. I decree that green pastures are opening up in front of you, opportunities you did not labor for, connections divinely orchestrated, doors that no man can shut because it is the Lord who opened them. I decree that every dry season in your business, in your career, in your finances is coming to an end. and streams in the desert are about to spring forth. I decree over [music] your health this morning, every sickness assigned to cut short days is canceled by the blood of Jesus. Every diagnosis that does not agree with the report of the Lord is reversed right now. I decree restoration to your body, restoration to your strength, restoration to every organ that has been under attack in the mighty name of Jesus. I decree over your family this morning, every prodigal child, every wandering son, every wandering daughter is being drawn back by the same shepherd who leaves the 99 to go after the one that is lost. I decree that the valley in your marriage is only a passage and you are walking through it into a place of restored love, restored communication, restored peace. I decree that the shadow of death hovering over any relationship in your life has no power [music] because greater is he that is in you than he that is in the world. I decree over your mind this morning every anxious thought, [music] every spirit of confusion, every torment that has kept you awake at night is silenced by the still waters of God's peace flooding your soul right now. I speak to every table the enemy has been trying to overturn before it even gets set. I say it is established. I speak to every plan of shame. The enemy prepared to embarrass you in front of your enemies. I say it is canled and instead you will be honored in the very presence of those who despised you. I decree fresh oil upon [music] your head this morning. If you have been feeling dry, if you have been feeling like your gifting has gone stale, if you have been feeling burnt out in ministry, burnt out at work, burnt out in your calling, I decree fresh fire, fresh anointing, fresh uncction falling upon you right now in Jesus name. Your cup is about to run over. Not trickle, not drip, but overflow. So much so that people around you will be blessed by the overflow of what God is doing in your life. Now, let us pray. And I need you to pray this like your life depends on it because in many ways it does. Lift your hands. Close your eyes if you need to, but let your spirit stay alert because we're about to go to war in prayer and then we're going to end in worship. Father, in the name of Jesus, we thank you this morning for being our shepherd. We thank you that you did not leave us as orphans. That you laid down your life for us. That you know our name. That you know the exact number of hairs on our head. That you know the exact burden weighing us down today. even the one we have not told anyone about. We come boldly not because we have earned it but because the blood of Jesus has made a way for us to come boldly to the throne of grace. Father, every spirit of lack assigned to my life in the mighty name of Jesus, [music] I command you to lose your hold now. Every generational chain of poverty, every ancestral [music] covenant of struggle, every altar in my family line that spoke against provision and increase, I fire you out by the blood of Jesus. Every power assigned to make me chase what God has already provided. I bind you now. I paralyze your operation in the name that is above every name. Holy Spirit, lead me beside still waters because I refuse to keep drinking from wells of anxiety, wells of comparison, wells of bitterness. I renounce every agreement I have made, knowingly or unknowingly with fear. And I receive your peace that surpasses all understanding to guard my heart and my mind in [music] Christ Jesus. Father, restore my soul. Every part of me that has been wounded by rejection, heal it now. Every part of me that has been shattered by disappointment, put it back together now. Every lie the enemy has planted about my identity, uproot it now by the truth of your word. That I am fearfully and wonderfully made. That I am the head and not the tail. That I am more than a conqueror through him who loved me. Lead me in paths of righteousness, not paths of compromise, not paths of shortcuts that [music] lead to destruction, but paths that carry your name and your glory. Let my life be a living epistle that convinces the doubting world that you are still God, that you still answer prayer, that you still heal, that you still deliver, that you still set free. Father, as I walk through whatever valley I am facing right now, whether it is a valley of health, a valley of finance, a valley of marriage, a valley of ministry, a valley of a weward child, a valley of grief over someone I lost. I declare I will fear no evil, for you are with me. I refuse to camp in this valley. I refuse to build a house here. I am only passing through. And on the other side of this valley [music] is testimony. On the other side of this valley is promotion. On the other side of this valley is a story that will save someone else's life. Let your rod defend me from every predator assigned to devour me while I am weak. Let your staff pull me back from every cliff the enemy has strategically placed on my path. Lord, prepare my table in the presence of my enemies. Let every mocker, every doubter, every family member who wrote me off, every colleague who underestimated me, every spirit of witchcraft assigned to monitor and hinder my breakthrough. Watch helplessly as you set up my elevation right in front of them. Anoint my head with fresh oil this morning. I refuse to operate in yesterday's anointing. I refuse to walk into today's assignment with an empty vessel. Fill me, overflow me until my cup runs over. Until the blessing on my life becomes too [music] much to contain, until it spills over onto my household, onto my children, onto my ministry, onto everyone connected to me by covenant and by blood. Father, let goodness and mercy [music] chase me down today. Let them overtake every fear that has been chasing me, every debt that has been chasing me, every sickness that has been chasing [music] me, every shame that has been chasing me. Let goodness and mercy run faster and catch up to every negative pursuit in my life. And let them escort me, not just today, but all the days of my life until I dwell in your house, in your presence, in your manifest glory, both now and forever more. And father I lift up every person receiving this word right now. Wherever they are, whatever situation surrounds them. If there is someone reading this in a hospital bed, I decree divine healing right now in Jesus name. If there is someone reading this facing eviction, facing bankruptcy, facing a business collapse, I decree divine provision and divine strategy right now in Jesus name. If there is someone whose marriage is on the brink, I decree divine restoration and reconciliation right now in Jesus name. If there is someone contemplating giving up, contemplating ending their life, contemplating walking away from everything, I decree the shepherd is right there with you in that valley and he's saying do not be afraid. I am with you. This shadow has no power to destroy you. Hold on. Your morning is coming. If there is someone who has drifted from God, someone who used to walk closely with him but life happened and the fire dimmed, this is your moment to come back. The shepherd has not stopped searching for you. He left the 99 to come looking for you specifically. Wherever you are, whatever you have done, however far you have wandered, say yes to him this morning. Say, Lord, be my shepherd again. Lead me back to green pastures. Lead me back to still waters. Restore my soul. I receive you aresh today, church. I feel something shifting in the spirit realm even as we speak this word. I feel chains breaking off finances. I feel healing virtue flowing into bodies. I feel marriage is being knit back together. I feel destinies being realigned. I feel fresh fire falling on cold, weary, burnt out believers. This is not just a devotional. This is an encounter. And I dare you to receive it not as information, but as impartation. Do not let this be words that pass through your ears and evaporate by lunchtime. Let it sink down into your spirit. Let it become the confession of your mouth throughout this week. Every morning when you wake up, before the news, before the messages, before the noise of the day, speak this psalm over your life. Say it out loud. The Lord is my shepherd. I shall not want. And as we close, hear this final word. Whatever attacked you yesterday does not have permission to follow you into today. Whatever tried to define you in your past does not have the final say over your future. You are not a victim of your circumstances. You are a sheep under the care of the chief shepherd. And he who began a good work in you is faithful to complete it. Somebody shout hallelujah one more time. Somebody give him praise like you already have the testimony in your hand because faith calls those things that be not as though they were. And this morning by faith I call you healed. I call you provided for. I call you restored. I call you delivered. I call you established. I call you more than a conqueror. Go from this place carrying this psalm like armor. Let it be the song on your lips when the enemy whispers doubt. Let it be your declaration when the report says one thing but the shepherd says another. Let it be your comfort in the valley and your shout in the place of victory. The Lord is your shepherd. You shall not want. He makes you lie down in green pastures. He leads you beside still waters. He restores your soul. He leads you in paths [music] of righteousness. Even in the valley, you fear no evil, for he is with you. He prepares your table. He anoints your head. Your cup runs over. Goodness and mercy are following you. And you will dwell in the house of the Lord forever. Receive it, walk in it, speak it until it becomes the atmosphere you live in. In the mighty, matchless, unshakable name of Jesus [music] Christ, we have prayed and we have declared it and so it is settled in heaven and it shall be established in the earth. Amen and amen. Before you go, hold this in your spirit a moment longer because heaven is not finished ministering to you yet. Somewhere in this reading, something in you loosened. Something in you exhaled. Something in you remembered what it felt like to trust again. And I want you to guard that feeling. Protect it like treasure because the enemy would try to steal it back with one phone call, one bad report, one delayed answer before the sun even sets today. Do not let him. When that moment comes, and it will come, open your mouth again and say it exactly as you said it here. The Lord is my shepherd. I shall not want. Let it become reflex. Let it become instinct. Let it become the first language your spirit speaks when trouble knocks. Carry this psalm into your kitchen, into your workplace, into your hospital appointment, into your business meeting, into your quiet moments of doubt at midnight. And let it be both your sword and your shelter. You were not brought to this world by accident this morning. The shepherd himself orchestrated this encounter because he has been waiting to remind you that you are not walking alone. You never have been and you never will be. Now rise up, wipe your eyes if you have been weeping. Straighten your shoulders, lift your countenance, and walk out from here different than you came in. Because a sheep who has heard the true voice of the shepherd can never again be satisfied wandering [music] aimlessly through life. Go in peace. Go in power. Go in expectation. The rest of your story has already been written in green pastures besides still waters. And it [music] is good.
